title: How to set a fence post that never wobbles

lines.show: You want a {g:fence} that stands straight.
So you push the post into a {r:shallow} hole.
One storm, and it {r:leans}.
So you dig {y:deeper}:
a {y:third} of the post goes underground.
But the hole is too {r:narrow}.
So you make it {y:three times} as wide as the post.
But the wet soil makes the bottom {r:rot}.
So you put {y:gravel} in the hole first,
so water can drain away.
Then you fill it with {y:concrete}.
But the post sets {r:crooked}.
So you check it with a {y:level}
and brace it until it's hard.
Rain collects around the {r:post}.
So you slope the concrete top {y:away} from the wood.
Then the {r:wind} pushes on the whole fence.
So you set a post about every {y:two meters}.
{y:Congratulations}.
You built a fence
that stands for {g:decades}.
